provider: Zenodo restricted-access records and secret links (working storage, not only an archive)

free_tier.stated: The same 50 GB per record and 150 GB per-account pool as the public path. Restricting the files neither reduces nor refunds the quota, so the capacity is identical
free_tier.notes: This record exists because the corpus held Zenodo's public deposit path and not its restricted one. They are the same quota with a different visibility flag, and the difference decides whether Zenodo can be a working set or only an archive

per_object_cap.stated: 50 GB per record on the default quota, with the 150 GB account pool distributable across records, and a hard 100 files per record
per_object_cap.notes: the 200 GB single-record figure is 50 GB plus the whole 150 GB pool, which requires distributing nothing else

retention.stated: A record cannot be deleted after 30 days. Restricted records carry the same rule, so a restricted record is as permanent as a public one and its quota is consumed monotonically

egress.terms: Free. A secret link grants 'Can view' on restricted or embargoed files of all current and future versions of that record, with optional expiry

interface_detail: the same deposition API; visibility is a field on the draft, set to restricted with an embargo date or a share link, and share links are managed from the record's Links tab
tooling: any HTTP client for the deposition and file APIs, working in the same way as the public path. There is no rclone backend, so uploads are plain HTTP PUT against a bucket URL
chaining: This is what turns Zenodo from a cold archive into something usable as a hot working set: the client can keep data off the public index while still holding 50 GB times N, and still read it programmatically with a token or a shared link. It composes with the 32-connection parallel read measured on the public path, because the throttle is per connection and not per visibility

limits.value: 50 GB per record on the default quota, 100 files per record
a record cannot be deleted after 30 days, restricted or not
100 requests per minute authenticated; 30 per minute on the search API

binding_note: The quota and the visibility are independent, so restricting a record buys privacy and no capacity. What binds is the 50 GB per-record ceiling, which sets the record count at about 410 for the 20 TiB archive whether the records are public or restricted
limits_note: Metadata is always public even when the files are restricted, so titles, descriptions and the minted DOI leak. That is a property of the visibility model and not a defect in this record

identity_cost.detail: an email address, GitHub or ORCID account.

reliability_note: Answers the working-storage question: workable for private data, but every record still carries permanently public metadata and a DOI, so it is a leaky private tier and not a private bucket. An interrupted upload leaves a Pending file that must be removed by hand
confidence_note: What would raise it is a probe of a restricted record read through a secret link

evidence.proved: 'Link sharing enables you to create a secret link which provides access to your record. The link can also have an expiry date.' and 'Can view: Grants access to view restricted/embargoed files of all current and future versions'
'the access right field has now been changed into a visibility field with two options (metadata is always public)'
each record comes with a default quota of 50 GB and an additional 150 GB allowance distributable across uploads, with no account-level total documented
records can be deleted by their owner within 30 days after publication, and outside that window only in justified cases

notes: A sub-finding of Zenodo, written as its own record because the corpus carried the public deposit path and not the restricted one, and the difference is the whole working-storage question. this is that record. It does not duplicate the main provider: the quota, the API and the lifecycle are the parent record's, and this one adds only the visibility field and what it costs

extras.what_the_parent_record_owns: the deposit API, the quota arithmetic, the 30-day window and the DOI behaviour
extras.what_this_record_owns: the visibility field, secret links, and the leak of metadata under a restricted record
